body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), can one construct a computable region \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n\) that is uniformly honest for \(\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\) over the binary-treatment fixed-grid model \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), contracts at the regular LP-value rate uniformly on every class with \(\min_{a,b:\tau_{a,b}^r(P)>0}\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\ge\kappa_n\), and attains a matching lower frontier as \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), while reverting to the nonshrinking behavior required by Theorem 3 at the boundary?
body.justification: The open content is an honest adaptation frontier between stable positive slack and disappearing branches.
body.gap: ChoRussell2024, KaidoMolinariStoye2019, and BaiEtAl2026 do not derive a completion-slack-indexed rate frontier for this exact-set map.
body.consumer: Such a region would replace the conservative projection region away from branch boundaries without contradicting the minimax impossibility at zero slack.
